records.text: An anonymous transplant coordinator said they had never seen thoracic trauma or hemorrhaging in a gunshot wound to the head or neck and that blunt-force chest trauma would be required, which they said would fit an exploding microphone theory.
records.speaker: Anonymous transplant coordinator email source (Ep iB-YtO3UZOg)

appearances.snippet: This next person said that they're a transplant coordinator, previously a scrub nurse in the OR for years, and I worked at a level one trauma center. I have scrubbed in on more gunshot wounds than I could ever count. ... I have never seen thoracic trauma or hemorrhaging, for that matter, in a gunshot wound to the head or neck. ... There would have to have been a blunt force trauma to the chest, which would make a lot of sense if his microphone exploded under his shirt.

verification.notes: The person's identity, transplant-coordinator role, and scrub-nurse experience are not authenticated. The claim relies on personal experience and an inferred exploding-microphone mechanism; general forensic literature says gunshot effects depend on projectile, velocity, direction, tissue, and temporary cavitation. No case-specific medical evidence establishes the proposed mechanism.

sources.title: Gunshot Wounds Forensic Pathology
sources.relevance: Forensic reference explains the variable tissue effects and evidence required for mechanism analysis.

records.text: An anonymous transplant coordinator said it takes at least eight hours for deep core body temperature to reach 40 degrees in a morgue cooler, while the reported timeline supported only about three hours in the morgue.
records.speaker: Anonymous transplant coordinator email source (Ep iB-YtO3UZOg)

appearances.snippet: Also, I was yelling at the TV when I was watching Baron's podcast the other day regarding the autopsy. It takes at least eight hours for your deep core body temperature to reach 40 degrees in a morgue cooler. ... The timeline would only support about three hours in the morgue depending on how much time Erika spent with him when she arrived, and that's if his body was ever taken to the morgue. Nothing about the case makes any sense and it's infuriating. I thank God for all of your hard work. Go Max. Justice for Charlie.

verification.notes: A forensic study measured refrigerated adult core temperatures at 3, 6, and 9 hours and found substantial individual variation affected by BMI and clothing; it does not establish a universal minimum of eight hours to reach 40°F. The claimed case timeline is also based on unauthenticated assumptions about morgue entry and autopsy timing. The exact universal threshold and case application are therefore unverifiable.

sources.title: Algor Mortis: An Erroneous Measurement Following Postmortem Refrigeration
sources.relevance: Peer-reviewed study documents variable cooling rates and the limited utility of refrigerated core temperature for timing.
